I'm 68, been farming my whole life here in Quzhou, only went to primary school. My family has 6 mu of good flat land. I don't read books about farming — I watch my neighbors and I remember what happened on my own fields.

This year I'll do the same double crop as always: winter wheat then summer maize on all 6 mu. I already planted the wheat last October with improved seed — the kind that doesn't fall over easy. Now in spring I need to take care of it. I'll put down about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu for the wheat total, split between the base fertilizer and the topdressing when it greens up. Also 6 kg of phosphorus and 4 kg of potash per mu. My neighbor tried using less fertilizer last year to save money, but his wheat was thin. I can't risk that — my wife and I need this income. I'll irrigate four times: green-up, jointing, heading, and grain filling. The tube well costs electricity, but without water there is no crop.

When wheat harvest comes in early June, I'll immediately plant summer maize with hybrid seed. Everyone uses hybrid now — you can't get good yield without it. I'll put 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 3 kg potash per mu for the maize. I'll irrigate twice: right after planting and at the big ear stage. If summer rains come, maybe I skip one, but I watch the sky. I spray pesticide twice for maize — herbicide once after emergence, and insecticide if I see worms. For wheat I spray twice too, mainly for weeds and rust.

For tillage, I rotary till before planting wheat in autumn. But after wheat harvest, there's no time to plough — only about one week before maize must go in. So I use no-tillage planting into the wheat stubble, like everybody does now. My nephew helps with the machine since I can't do heavy work like I used to.

I expect about 480 kg per mu for wheat and 520 kg per mu for maize. Last year I got close to that. At my age I don't chase miracles — I want a reliable harvest that pays for my grandchildren's school things and leaves something in the jar. This plan has worked for twenty years, and I'll stick with it until the land or my body tells me otherwise.
